title: Case study: photo sharing (Instagram)

kcs.statement: Clients upload photos straight to object storage using a short-lived pre-signed upload URL from the API. Large bytes never pass through the app servers.
After upload, an event on a queue triggers workers that generate thumbnails in several sizes. The post becomes visible only after processing completes.
For photo apps, media storage and CDN egress dominate cost: 100M uploads a day at 2 MB is about 200 TB of new storage per day before replication.

problem_ideas: Compute 1-year storage for 50M uploads a day at 3 MB with 3 thumbnails of 100 KB each.
Estimate CDN egress if each photo is viewed 50 times at the 300 KB size.
Sequence the upload flow: get URL, PUT to storage, notify API, process, publish.
A worker crashes halfway through generating thumbnails. Make the job safe to retry.
Explain why proxying uploads through app servers limits horizontal scaling.
Decide where 'like' counts are stored and how they avoid becoming a hot key.
